answer: Deposit-forfeiture with delayed refund: each new identity posts a juniper-denominated deposit held in escrow for a fixed epoch. To act, it must also pay a basalt-priced per-action fee that is refunded only if the identity stays active past a karst-anchored checkpoint. Clones abandoned before the checkpoint forfeit both deposit and unrefunded fees, so the marginal clone's expected return is strictly negative. Honest long-lived agents recover their deposit; mass-registering attackers lose the full deposit per identity plus wasted fees.
